notes: Architectural adherence: The event bus is used correctly for task.assigned, task.statusChanged, and comment.added. However, rule #1 (no direct service-to-service calls) is violated in router.ts handleCreateComment, which calls both this.users.get() and this.tasks.get() to enrich the notification payload before passing data to CommentService — this is cross-service data access orchestrated outside the bus. While the Router is the HTTP entry point (rule #3 satisfied), the enrichment logic bleeds service concerns into the router. The try/catch in publish() is placed outside the setImmediate callback, meaning errors thrown inside the callback are never caught. Completeness: All five services are present with their own files. CRUD for users, projects, tasks, comments is implemented. Events task.assigned, task.statusChanged, comment.added are published. Demo script exists and exercises the main flows. Missing: comment.added notification is sent only to the author (acknowledged as a limitation in a code comment), not to the task assignee or project members — the notification semantics are incomplete. The event bus publish wraps callbacks in setImmediate but the try/catch surrounds setImmediate scheduling, not the callback execution, so subscriber errors are silently swallowed without the comment being accurate. No GET /notifications/:id endpoint. No update endpoint for comments (minor, not required). handleGetTask/handleGetProject use req.url!.split('/')[2] which breaks for paths like /tasks/id/assign or /tasks/id/status (split index 2 is correct but fragile — works here because sub-routes use different handlers). Code quality: TypeScript types are clean and consistent. Return type Task | null | Error is an unusual and non-idiomatic pattern; a discriminated union or thrown exception would be cleaner. URL parsing mixes URL API and raw req.url.split() inconsistently. The setImmediate/try-catch bug is a logic error. The 'old' variable in assign() is computed but never used. Routing is a long if-chain with no abstraction. Constraint compliance: Rule 1 violated (router queries UserService and TaskService to pass metadata to CommentService). Rule 4 (forward-only transitions) is correctly enforced. Rule 5 (no npm deps) satisfied — only Node.js built-ins used. Rule 6 (each service in own file) satisfied. Rules 2 and 3 are mostly satisfied. Two rules partially violated brings the score down.
